title: Put a blood-pressure cuff on a mannequin's upper arm: wrap it round, close it over the artery mark, then let go
instruction: Wrap the blood-pressure cuff round the mannequin's left upper arm with its arrow on the marked line and its lower edge 2 to 4 cm above the elbow crease, fasten it, then let go.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; BLS OEWS May 2025: 1,448,910 employed) record vital signs many times a shift (O*NET core task: vital signs "such as temperature, blood pressure, pulse, or respiration rate, as directed by medical or nursing staff"), and every blood-pressure reading starts with fitting the cuff. The cuff is a floppy strap: one hand has to lay its start end on the arm while the other brings the free end round, snug, and presses the hook-and-loop closed with the artery mark over the artery and the lower edge 2-3 cm above the elbow crease.
setup: A display-mannequin left arm lies fixed along x in front of the robot, its axis 100 mm above the table on two grey props: a box under the shoulder end and a foam wedge under the forearm. The upper arm tapers from 55 to 49 mm radius (325 mm round the middle, estimated: the mannequin listing publishes chest 36.5 in and waist 29.5 in but no arm circumference, so it is measured at mid-arm before a trial and must be within the cuff's printed 25-34 cm), its underside 45-51 mm above the table and clear between the props. A dark elbow-crease ring marks x 0.35 m, and a dark 4 mm artery line runs along the top of the upper arm. An adult size-11 cuff (520 x 140 x 3 mm, 0.10 kg, estimated) lies flat on the table across under the arm, skin face up, centred under the upper arm 100 mm above the crease; its start end (grey hook patch on the outer face of the first 220 mm) is on the left-arm side and its free end (loop face on the skin face of the last 100 mm) on the right-arm side. Each 20 mm end piece is propped curled up so a gripper can pinch it (a staging aid: on the real cuff each end piece is folded up about 80 deg by hand and held by one strip of masking tape across the fold on its inner side; a real flat cuff is picked up by its edge). A white ARTERY arrow is printed on the outer face 100 mm from the free end, pointing to the cuff's lower edge. One fixed layout; arms start at the ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial; the run ends with full credit once 1.0 has held for 1 s. 1.0: the closure is engaged, the cuff goes one full turn round the arm and is snug (no part of it more than 10 mm off the skin, or off the layer under it), the artery arrow faces out and is at most 20 mm (along the skin) from the artery line, the cuff's lower edge is 20 to 40 mm above the elbow crease, and both grippers' tool points and pad tips are at least 3 cm from the cuff. 0.6: engaged and snug, but the arrow or the edge height is out of range or a gripper is still on the cuff. 0.3: one full turn round the arm with no part more than 30 mm off, and not closed or not snug. 0 otherwise. The closure engages only when at least 60 mm of the loop face lies within 6 mm of the hook face and a gripper with closed fingers presses that lying loop face: pad tip within 2 mm of it and the loop segment under it pushed at least 0.15 mm toward the arm since the pad arrived, for 0.3 s; a graze, a stand-off, a pad hovering or resting without pushing, or a pinched or dragged cuff does not close it. It opens again, with no hand on it, on a peel of more than 15 mm with more than 4 N or a shear of more than 10 N. Once engaged, the fastening holds only the hinges that span the overlap (the ones under the pressed loop face); every other hinge keeps its own fabric stiffness. Shortcuts that score 0: doing nothing, sweeping the cuff, lifting and dropping it, half a wrap.
reset_notes: Peel the cuff open, lay it flat across under the arm with the start end on the left-arm side, fold each end piece up about 80 deg and tape the fold (one strip of masking tape on its inner side), and set it 100 mm above the crease. If the measured mid-arm circumference is outside the cuff's 25-34 cm range, use the cuff size that covers it.
fidelity: Isaac Sim 6.1 rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz control). The cuff is 26 rigid 20 mm segments on weakly sprung hinges (estimated); its end pieces are propped curled as a staging aid; it starts under the arm. Hook-and-loop is task logic: a closed fist pressing the overlap (within 2 mm, cuff pushed >= 0.15 mm) for 0.3 s locks the overlap hinges at that angle, the rest keep fabric stiffness; a peel over 4 N or shear over 10 N opens it (estimated). Bladder, air and stretch are not modelled.
